added_models.model: Crohn's patient mucosal organ cultures and lamina propria T cells from anti-TNF non-responders (anti-IL23p19 ex vivo)

efficacy.model: Crohn's patient mucosal organ cultures and lamina propria T cells from anti-TNF non-responders (anti-IL23p19 ex vivo)
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC6580782). The ex-vivo antibody was a commercial anti-IL23p19 (R&D Systems), not a class member.
efficacy.note: Apoptosis-resistant TNFR2+IL23R+ T cells expand in anti-TNF non-responders; ex-vivo anti-IL23p19 induced their apoptosis, naming IL-23 as the target in that group.
efficacy.short: IL-23 named as target in anti-TNF failures
efficacy.quote: These findings identify IL-23 as a suitable molecular target in patients with Crohn's disease refractory to anti-TNF therapy.
efficacy.judgement: Opener at first use (epub 2018-05-30). A patient-level system: patient mucosal organ cultures and LPMCs sorted by anti-TNF response, with anti-IL23p19 and IL-23 added ex vivo. Separate from the mouse and genetic tracks because it is a different system with its own prediction (which patients, not whether the class works). model_filed false: neither bundled FDA review cites it.

efficacy.model: Crohn's patient mucosal organ cultures and lamina propria T cells from anti-TNF non-responders (anti-IL23p19 ex vivo)
efficacy.magnitude_basis: ex-vivo T-cell apoptosis / IL-23-axis readout versus phase 2 remission in anti-TNF-experienced patients
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text read. The source is the model paper and itself states the comparison, so model_src carries the patient side (Feagan 2017, with Sands 2017 MEDI2070 in patient_trials); both trials were public (April 2017) before the model paper.
efficacy.note: The paper sets its ex-vivo finding beside the 2017 risankizumab and MEDI2070 phase 2 results in anti-TNF-experienced patients and calls them concordant.
efficacy.short: Reproduces phase 2 success in anti-TNF failures
efficacy.quote: Recently published trials showed that risankizumab and MEDI2070, specific inhibitors for IL-23 p19, were remarkably effective in anti-TNF refractory patients with CD.
efficacy.judgement: Retrodiction (decision 10): the phase 2 trials in largely anti-TNF-experienced patients (Feagan 2017 epub 2017-04-12, 93% anti-TNF-experienced; Sands 2017 epub 2017-04-05) were known when the paper framed its aim around them, so retro, not same. The paper itself notes the trials did not compare anti-TNF-naive with -experienced patients, so the match is at population level, direction only.

patient_trials.quote: Ten (24%) of 41 patients who received 200 mg risankizumab had clinical remission (9·0%, -8·3 to 26·2; p=0·31) and 15 (37%) of 41 who received the 600 mg dose (20·9%, 2·6 to 39·2; p=0·0252).

The primary outcome, clinical response (either a 100-point decrease in CD Activity Index score from baseline or clinical remission, defined as CD Activity Index score <150) at week 8 occurred in 49.2% of patients receiving MEDI2070 (n = 59) compared with 26.7% receiving placebo (n = 60; absolute difference, 22.5%; 95% confidence interval, 5.6%-39.5%; P = .010).

efficacy.model: Crohn's patient mucosal organ cultures and lamina propria T cells from anti-TNF non-responders (anti-IL23p19 ex vivo)
efficacy.magnitude_basis: ex-vivo prediction that IL-23 blockade works in anti-TNF-refractory patients versus placebo-adjusted CDAI remission in MOTIVATE (biologic failures)
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading of D'Haens 2022 (Europe PMC rendering; the abstract CI dashes are written as hyphens there). Paired by me; D'Haens does not cite the ex-vivo work.
efficacy.note: MOTIVATE, run only in biologic (mostly anti-TNF) failures, met both coprimaries with risankizumab 600 mg: remission 42% vs 20%, endoscopic response 29% vs 11%.
efficacy.quote: In MOTIVATE, CDAI clinical remission rate was 42% (22%, 13-31; 80/191) with risankizumab 600 mg and 40% (21%, 12-29; 77/191) with risankizumab 1200 mg versus 20% (37/187) with placebo
efficacy.judgement: The first prospective test after the retrodiction (decision 10): MOTIVATE's result (registry 2022-06-14, Lancet May 2022) postdates the 2018 prediction, and its population is exactly the one the model named. Scored same, patient-level, but weakly: the cellular marker (TNFR2+IL23R+ expansion) was never measured in trial patients, and the model's prediction was itself shaped by the phase 2 data, so this is population-level concordance, direction only. Mirikizumab VIVID-1 (2024) and ADVANCE's biologic-failure stratum would add nothing to the status.

patient_trials.quote: Ten (24%) of 41 patients who received 200 mg risankizumab had clinical remission (9·0%, -8·3 to 26·2; p=0·31) and 15 (37%) of 41 who received the 600 mg dose (20·9%, 2·6 to 39·2; p=0·0252).

The primary outcome, clinical response (either a 100-point decrease in CD Activity Index score from baseline or clinical remission, defined as CD Activity Index score <150) at week 8 occurred in 49.2% of patients receiving MEDI2070 (n = 59) compared with 26.7% receiving placebo (n = 60; absolute difference, 22.5%; 95% confidence interval, 5.6%-39.5%; P = .010).
In MOTIVATE, CDAI clinical remission rate was 42% (22%, 13-31; 80/191) with risankizumab 600 mg and 40% (21%, 12-29; 77/191) with risankizumab 1200 mg versus 20% (37/187) with placebo

added_models.model: Sponsor population-PK / exposure-response dose model from phase 2 (risankizumab; mirikizumab pooled)

dose.model: Sponsor population-PK / exposure-response dose model from phase 2 (risankizumab; mirikizumab pooled)
dose.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC6373392). The paper reports PK only and says the Crohn's exposure-response reports are 'planned'; the phase 2 exposure-response read that chose 600 mg IV for phase 3 (started May 2017) is public only through the FDA review.
dose.note: Phase I/II popPK model (incl. Crohn's phase 2) underpinned the exposure-response read that picked 600 mg IV for phase 3; no phase 3 result yet.
dose.quote: A two-compartment model with first-order absorption and elimination described the pharmacokinetics of risankizumab.
dose.judgement: Opens the in-silico track at its first public date (PubMed 2018-08-21; print March 2019). One track for the sponsors' phase 2 popPK/exposure-response dose models (AbbVie risankizumab; Lilly mirikizumab, CTS 2025) under the identity rule: same system class, same prediction (the phase 2 exposure plateau fixes the induction dose). Surrogate mouse dosing (15 mg/kg IP) set no human target, so this is the only model that stated one.

dose.model: Sponsor population-PK / exposure-response dose model from phase 2 (risankizumab; mirikizumab pooled)
dose.magnitude_basis: phase 2 exposure-response-selected induction dose (600 mg IV, predicted Cavg 60.5 mg/L) versus the approved induction dose (600 mg IV); 1200 mg added nothing
dose.confidence_note: Quote from the bundled 761262 IntegratedR text (section 14.4.2). The exposure-response report the review cites (R&D/20/1614) is dated 2020 and pools phase 2 and 3; whether a formal model, rather than the phase 2 dose-response itself, chose 600 mg in 2017 is not stated. Decision 16 does not apply: no tolerability margin was stated by this model.
dose.note: Phase 3 reached the ER-selected 600 mg IV exposures and both coprimaries were met; 1200 mg added nothing, so the model's target was enough.
dose.short: ER-selected 600 mg IV held in phase 3
dose.quote: Model predictions together with observed data indicated that the efficacy may have reached a plateau at 600 mg IV induction regimen with no substantial added benefit from the 1200 mg IV induction regimen.
dose.reason: 600 mg IV reached; phase 3 confirmed plateau
dose.judgement: Dose table case 'reached, drug worked': the regimen the phase 2 exposure-response read chose (600 mg IV at weeks 0, 4, 8) was given in ADVANCE/MOTIVATE (registry 2022-06-14 and 2022-07-06), met both coprimaries, and the 1200 mg arm showed no added benefit, so the target was enough. Maintenance was not model-chosen (no phase 2 dose-ranging; 180 vs 360 mg SC showed no dose-response). The hepatotoxicity at this exposure is counted once, in safety on the cynomolgus track, because this model stated no margin. Tier-1 corroboration that changes no status: Suleiman 2023 CPT (doi 10.1002/cpt.2831, epub 2023-01-20, abstract-level) says the same from phase 2+3 data, and Lilly's mirikizumab model (doi 10.1111/cts.70320, 2025) found VIVID-1's 900 mg result 'aligned with SERENITY'.

considered_not_added: IL-23p19-knockout colitis (Yen 2006, doi 10.1172/JCI21404): a genetic mouse model never compared with a member's patient results; no admissible comparison, so no track.

Anti-CD40 SCID colitis with the risankizumab surrogate PR-963484 (BLA 761262 s5.1): rule question 3 decided as one model_id with T-cell-transfer colitis (mouse-colitis-anti-p19-surrogate). Under this run's identity rule a separate track needs a genuinely different system AND a different prediction; the innate (anti-CD40) and adaptive (T-cell transfer) models differ as systems but make the same prediction with the same surrogate (anti-p19 treats mouse colitis, so the class treats Crohn's), so they stay one track.

Mirikizumab surrogate LSN2479016 murine colitis, Steere 2023 J Pharmacol Exp Ther (doi 10.1124/jpet.122.001512, title only): a better tier-1 model_src for the existing mouse track, not a new system; the draft is not edited from this file.

Brazikumab baseline serum IL-22 responder marker (Sands 2017) and the pharmacometric model built on it (CPT Pharmacometrics Syst Pharmacol 2023, doi 10.1002/psp4.13044, epub 2023-10-06, abstract read): the model is fitted to the phase 2a data it describes, not compared with them, and its prospective test INTREPID (NCT03759288) was stopped without outcome data; a patient biomarker, no track, per instruction.

Mirikizumab popPK/exposure-response model (Clin Transl Sci 2025, doi 10.1111/cts.70320, abstract read: VIVID-1 900 mg 'aligned with SERENITY'): folded into poppk-er-phase2-dose-model as the same system class and prediction; it changes no status, so no entry.
Guselkumab: not in the members list (brazikumab, mirikizumab, risankizumab); not widened.

Ustekinumab-based patient predictors (IL23R pharmacogenetics review doi 10.3390/ph19091428; serum IL-12/23 early-response predictor, Front Immunol 2026 doi 10.3389/fimmu.2026.1753914): anti-p40, not a member; set aside under decision 13.

Patient-derived organoids, mucosal explants dosed with a member, and humanized-mouse colitis: no member study found in any sweep; IL-23 acts on immune cells, so no epithelial organoid track is expected.

Cross-indication bridging (psoriasis and UC PK used for the Crohn's regimen): a patient result in another indication, not a model system; the draft's dose cell already records that Crohn's dosing came from psoriasis PK and the human phase 2.

Mouse colonic IL-23/IL-17 cytokine PD versus Visvanathan 2018 patient biopsies: already the mouse track's engagement entry; the ex-vivo track's apoptosis readout was never measured in dosed patients, so it gets no engagement entry.
